  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Loca l, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We wi ll inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We sha ll refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised .

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and officia l lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

 Background:
On March 4 , 2020, the Park and Recreation Commission (Commission) approved the
draft Dedication Plaque and Paver Policy (Policy) and recommended that this matter be
presented to the City Council for approval. On March 11 , 2020, the City Council approved
the Policy. Applications for the paver dedications were mailed to all residents on April 30,
2020, indicating an application deadline of May 21 , 2020. Additionally, the application
acceptance period and Policy was posted on the City's website and social media sites.

As of May 21 , 2020, 26 paver applications were received. Upon verifying the information
on the application and wording to be displayed on the pavers, the engraver advised staff
that the pavers would be completed by July 22, 2020. An additional 16 paver applications
were submitted through July 81h and these dedications were engraved with the initial
order. All of the pavers, including the engraved pavers, were installed on July 21 , 2020.

This project is moving along and is anticipated to be completed by mid-September. The
Policy was prepared based on engraving quantity information provided by the engraver.
Based on staff's experience with the initial application process, it is now necessary to
amend the Policy to ensure the structural integrity of the removal and replacement of the
pavers. The Public Works Services Department will be responsible for installing the new
paver dedications and is recommending minimal disturbance to the pavers, as the sand
grout has been compacted to ensure stability of the pavers. In an effort to minimize the
disturbance, staff is recommending that the new dedication pavers be installed on an
annual basis, as opposed to an ongoing basis throughout the year. This will also serve
as an annual commemoration of the construction of the memorial garden. The pavers
will be installed by the Public Works Services Department in late April/early May, pending
receipt of the pave rs from the engraver. Staff is recommending the following sections be
amended :

   IRWINDALE

Dedication Plaque and Paver
  Policy

  Date: March 11, 2020
  Amended: August 5, 2020
 1. SCOPE

  The policy covers dedication plaques and pavers on City owned land, including
  streets, reserves or parks. All new plaques and pavers will be required to conform to
  this policy.

2. PURPOSE

  The purpose of this policy is to provide a framework for management of existing
  plaques and pavers, installation of new plaques or pavers and assessment of new
  requests for plaques and pavers within the public space in the City of Irwindale.

3. DEFINITIONS

  Application Period - Applications will be accepted on an annual basis from March 1
  through and including March 31 .

  Memorial - An object established in memory of a person, association , anniversary or
  event  and  includes  a  monument.

  Open Space - Open space refers to all land owned and/or managed by the City of
  Irwindale that is zoned Public Park and is available for public access. Typically open
  space includes parks, gardens, trails, habitat corridors, utilities reserves , foreshores,
  waterways, sportsgrounds and conservation reserves. It does not include vacant
  municipal  land  zoned  for  other  purposes.

  Plaque - flat tablet of metal, stone or other material which includes text or images
  which commemorate a person, event or historical information relative to the location or
  a new public artwork of significance.

  Public Place - Public Place refers to road reserves, Municipal Buildings, streetscapes
  and other land that are owned and/or managed by the City.

4. BACKGROUND

  4.1  Pubic space is a significant part of the City's social and cultural heritage and
  makes a valued recreational, environmental and aesthetic contribution for people who
  live, work, and recreate in the City. Dedication plaques and pavers provide recognition
  and can contribute to an understanding of significant events or persons closely
  associated with the City's history.

  4.2  The Irwindale City Council recognizes that plaques and memorials provide
  recognition and are important in celebrating significant historical events and persons or
  organizations closely associated with the leadership, cultural and social development
  of the City.
   4.3  The memorial garden at Irwindale Park will allow community members to
  commemorate a person , group, association or event. Dedication pavers will be
  available by request for anybody wishing to honor such person, group, association or
  event.

  4.4  The City Council Chamber seating includes a mounted plaque on the armrest of
  each chair. The engraving of the Plaques in the City Council Chamber will be available
  by request for anybody who desires to commemorate a person , group, association or
  event.

  4.5  Any decision regarding Plaques and pavers needs to consider the balance
  between the desire to commemorate events or individuals and the ongoing enjoyment
  of uncluttered public space.

  This policy will provide a consistent and standard procedure for assisting requests in
  relation to new plaques and pavers.

5. GENERAL PRINCIPLES

  5.1  Requests for engraving of a Plaque in the Council Chamber or the Memorial
  Garden pavers shall be made by filling out an application (Attachment "A"). Plaques
  and pavers will be reviewed , approved and assigned by City staff based on availability.

  5.2  The City Council does not guarantee to retain plaques or memorials in
  perpetuity. Generally, a plaque or memorial will be retained in place for as long as
  practicable, in the City Council's discretion, with the following exceptions:
  • the area in which the item is sited is to be redeveloped ; or
  • ongoing maintenance costs are prohibitive; or
  • in the case of a plaque or paver, the asset to which it is attached has reached
  the end of its useful life; or
  • the condition of the plaque or memorial is poor.

  5.3  If a plaque or paver is removed due to any of the reasons above, the City
  Council will not guarantee replacement of the plaque or paver, however replacement
  plaques or pavers of similar or different style or form may be considered . All
  reasonable efforts will be made to identify, contact and advise relevant stakeholders
  (including family members) prior to removal or replacement.

  5.4  The design and wording for the plaque and paver must be submitted with the
  application . All wording and design must be approved by the City Manager or his
  designee.

  5.5  The number of lines of text allowable will be in accordance with any
  recommendations put forward by the plaque and paver manufacturer.

  5.6  The City of Irwindale shall not be liable for damage to the plaques or pavers
  which are eroded or damaged by weather, the elements, thieves, vandals,
   trespassers, ordinary wear and tear, or standard maintenance performed by
  employees of the City of Irwindale.

6.  Maintenance and Repair

  The long-term care and maintenance of a plaque or paver is important to both the
  donor and the City. The City has the duty to maintain the donation until removal
  and/or relocation is necessary.

  Maintenance by the City of Irwindale will be limited to varnishing of the plaque and
  minor repairs to the plaque or paver. The City of Irwindale will not be held responsible
  for damaged plaques resulting from vandalism or any other condition or act that would
  require replacement. Should the City of Irwindale determine that an existing plaque
  needs replacement, all associated costs will be at the expense of the donor, should
  donor elect to replace the plaque.

  The City reserves the right to remove a donated plaque or paver if, in the City's
  discretion , the maintenance and repair cost are too high.

7.  COSTS

  7.1  All costs associated with the design, construction, installation and maintenance
  of plaques or memorials are to be paid by the person making the request for the
  plaque engraving or paver. Once approved, installation of any plaque or paver must be
  undertaken by City staff. Installed plaques and pavers will become the property of City
  of Irwindale. Maintenance of plaques and memorials must be undertaken by City.

  Exact cost of pavers or plaques will vary by size and updated on an annual basis per
  the rates approved by the City Council (Attachment "A").

  7.2  Pavers will only be ordered in quantities of four. The City will not place an order
  for a paver until a total of four applications have been received and approved. The City
  will place the engraved paver order when a minimum quantity of four (4) paver
  applications has been received by the City during the Application Period . This is the
  minimum quantity order established by the engraver.

  7.3  If the minimum quantity is not met during the Application Period . then the
  approved applications will be carried forward to the next Application Period. These
  applications will continue to be carried forward until the minimum quantity is met. As a
  result. those applications that are carried forward will be subject to the annual rate
  increase. determined by the engraver.
